So, i'm new to reloading. I mixed up a batch of .308s with 168 gr Sierra spear points, 42.5 grains of IMR4064, R-P brass with Winchester primers and an OAL of 2.740'', the groups were horrible. @ 100 yards I was shooting an 18 inch group after 6 Rounds. I feel like I missed something critical. Please tell me what I should do to troubleshoot the remaining rounds or give me some guidance on what I should try for better consistency.

what makes an accurate or inaccurate load depends a lot on the harmonics of the specific gun as the bullet travels down the barrel during the firing process. I bet your loads are either too hot or not hot enough. try researching and finding different loads to try and make up a few of each. then go to the range and test them out. also shoot some factory rounds through the gun as a control, just to make sure the gun isnt the problem.

One critical element when feeling out recipes for any caliber is focusing on good marksmenship. I do not mean to insult but that is were one should start.

Next, imr 4064 can get a little wonky with short action cases (my personal experience) so the inconsistency could be to that. As u/tippyc said each rifle has its sweet spot for powders and charge weights. They also have a sweet spot for stand-off (the distance from the ogive of the bullet to the lands of the rifling).

For non-magnum 30 cals I really have good luck with imr 4350, especially with parents cases being the 308 or 30-06.

Also, if you are using a set of brass for only 1 rifle, only neck size do not full length size, this helps keep neck tension and length very close between cases.

Of course, be as absolute as possible to when it comes to charge weights.
